gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the brands' 'AI bird ID' claims on the same basis. Since 2 November 2026, Birdfy's free plan identifies species automatically and without limit on its feeders' videos. Birdbuddy's free plan identifies a bird only when you pick a photo and ask. Getting automatic ID on a Birdbuddy for three years costs about $297 in fees ($98.99/yr Family Premium), which takes the $199 Birdbuddy Home to about $496 against $199.99 all-in for the Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K.
standout_why: Reviewed (cited, 2026-11-06) says Birdbuddy Home's automatic ID needs Family Premium at $98.99/yr, so that half is already out there. But the same page says the Birdfy Feeder 2 Pro needs a subscription after a 7-day trial ($79.99/yr), which Birdfy dropped on 2 November. ChatGPT's answer credits WIRED (cited, 2026-11-02) with Birdfy's 'free automatic AI identification', but WIRED blocked my fetch, so I could not check what it says. Feeder Field (2026-10-07) calls Birdfy's ID terms 'Unclear' and quotes the old trial. PlumageDispatch has a 3-year fee table but lists 'Bird Buddy basic AI' at $0. Birdbuddy's own pages say that free tier is manual-only. No rival gives Birdfy's free-tier limits (10 Photo IDs a day, 20-second clips kept 30 days), and none prices 3 years of automatic ID side by side. Digital Camera World's buying guide (updated 2026-10-09) does not mention the change.
decides: This supports Birdfy as the main pick for a shopper who wants birds named automatically: every Birdfy feeder on our page now has unlimited species ID on the free plan. Birdbuddy's free plan names a bird only when you select a photo, so its row should say 'manual on free plan; automatic = +$98.99/yr' and not 'AI ID'. Birdbuddy stays the pick only for shoppers who will pay for its app. It also means we should drop any 'lifetime AI' premium or trial caveat from the Birdfy rows.
